controls.label: Monochrome
controls.qualification: LROC WAC global morphologic mosaic v1.3, 32 pixels/degree, mapped to the 1,737.4 km lunar reference sphere.
controls.notes: LROC WAC 643 nm photography, mapped from observations in 2009–2011. Crater shadows are part of the photographs; the Shadows control adds scene lighting. Gray grid marks missing data. Brightness is adjusted for display.

controls.label: Midnight temperature
controls.qualification: False-color bolometric temperature fitted to local midnight from Diviner observations in 2009–2022. Colors span 80–140 K, with endpoint colors beyond that range. Gray grid marks missing data and latitudes beyond ±70°. This combines many nights; it is not a current temperature map.
controls.notes: False-color bolometric temperature fitted to local midnight from Diviner observations in 2009–2022. Colors span 80–140 K, with endpoint colors beyond that range. Gray grid marks missing data and latitudes beyond ±70°. This combines many nights; it is not a current temperature map.

controls.label: Heat anomalies
controls.qualification: False-color difference between Diviner bolometric temperature at slope-adjusted midnight and a model of typical lunar soil. Blue is cooler and red warmer than the model; colors span −10 to +10 K. Observations cover 2009–2022 within ±70°; gray grid marks unavailable data. Residual terrain effects remain, and warm colors do not establish geothermal activity.

controls.label: Rock abundance
controls.qualification: Surface area covered by rocks, inferred with a rock-and-soil thermal model from Diviner observations in 2009–2022 at slope-adjusted midnight. Colors span 0–2%; larger fractions share the brightest color. Gray grid marks missing or physically invalid values and latitudes beyond ±70°. This estimates rock area, not individual boulder counts.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.qualification: LRO LOLA LDEM16 numeric elevation above a 1,737.4 km sphere
controls.notes: Numeric LOLA elevation above a 1,737.4 km reference sphere. Colors represent −12 to +12 km; this gridded laser-altimetry product includes interpolation and does not displace the globe or represent current illumination.

controls.label: Crust
controls.qualification: NASA GRAIL crustal-thickness map with shaded relief
controls.notes: Crustal thickness inferred from GRAIL gravity and lunar topography under assumed crust and mantle densities. This is an interior model shown with shaded relief, not a direct observation of the crust.

controls.label: Gravity
controls.qualification: False-color GRAIL free-air gravity anomaly from the GRGM1200A field summed to degree 660, in mGal on a 1,738 km sphere. Blue is weaker and red stronger gravity than a uniform Moon; colors span −400 to +400 mGal and stronger values share the end colors. Topography is not removed, so high ground reads positive. Mission data 2012; the whole globe is covered.

controls.label: Bouguer gravity
controls.qualification: False-color GRAIL Bouguer disturbance from the GRGM1200A field summed to degree 660, in mGal: gravity after the pull of LOLA topography, taken as rock of 2,500 kg/m³, is removed. Colors span −600 to +600 mGal and stronger values share the end colors. Red usually marks dense mantle nearer the surface; mare basalt is not removed. The Crust view is a model derived from maps like this one.

controls.label: Silicate signature
controls.qualification: Diviner Christiansen-feature wavelength with improved viewing-geometry and space-weathering corrections; composition proxy within ±70° latitude
controls.notes: Diviner measures a thermal-infrared emissivity peak related to silicate composition. This 2021 map corrects viewing geometry and space weathering. Colors span 8.0–8.5 µm; values outside that range share endpoint colors. This is a composition proxy, not mineral abundance; residual topographic effects remain, especially above 50° latitude. Gray grid marks missing observations and latitudes beyond ±70°.

controls.label: Tiny iron particles
controls.qualification: Submicroscopic metallic iron (SMFe), a fitted space-weathering parameter. This release uses seven model amounts from 0.5 to 7 weight percent; these are spectral-model choices, not measured soil samples. Kaguya MI derived map, May 2016 release, within ±50° latitude. Colors show modeled values; gray grid marks missing data and the unmapped polar regions. Missing or negative fit-quality values are rejected; no confidence threshold is invented. The display samples native cells without filling gaps.
controls.notes: Solar-wind particles and tiny impacts change exposed lunar soil. Very small metallic iron particles help darken it and change its reflected light. Estimated percentage by weight. The model chooses from 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 7%; yellow means more iron. Kaguya measured reflected sunlight in nine wavelength bands. A model compared those measurements with mixtures of minerals. This quantity is called submicroscopic metallic iron (SMFe). The seven amounts are model choices. They are not laboratory measurements of samples collected at each location. 50° south to 50° north. Gray grid marks the polar regions, missing measurements, or cells without a usable model fit.

controls.label: Mineral grain size
controls.qualification: The spectral model chooses between 17 and 200 µm plagioclase grains. These two model classes are not a continuous measurement of individual grains. Kaguya MI derived map, May 2016 release, within ±50° latitude. Colors show modeled values; gray grid marks missing data and the unmapped polar regions. Missing or negative fit-quality values are rejected; no confidence threshold is invented. The display samples native cells without filling gaps.
controls.notes: The size of a mineral grain affects how it reflects light. This map shows which of two plagioclase grain sizes fits better. 17 µm = 0.017 mm; 200 µm = 0.2 mm. These are two separate choices, not a continuous size scale. Kaguya measured reflected sunlight in nine wavelength bands. A model compared those measurements with mixtures of minerals. It tries these two sizes for plagioclase. The model does not measure individual grains. Other minerals keep the model’s fixed grain size. 50° south to 50° north. Gray grid marks the polar regions, missing measurements, or cells without a usable model fit.

controls.label: Mineral composition
controls.qualification: Spectral mixture estimate of plagioclase abundance by weight. The authors warn that subdued absorption bands in mature soil can overestimate plagioclase; compare optical maturity. Kaguya MI derived map, May 2016 release, within ±50° latitude. Colors show modeled values; gray grid marks missing data and the unmapped polar regions. Missing or negative fit-quality values are rejected; no confidence threshold is invented. The display samples native cells without filling gaps.
controls.notes: Plagioclase is an ingredient of rock, also found in granite on Earth. It is abundant in the Moon’s ancient highland crust. Percentage by weight: 50% means half the modeled material by weight. Yellow means more; dark blue means less. Kaguya measured reflected sunlight in nine wavelength bands. A model compared those measurements with mixtures of minerals. Weathered soil weakens the mineral signal and can make this estimate too high. Compare the Surface weathering map. 50° south to 50° north. Gray grid marks the polar regions, missing measurements, or cells without a usable model fit.

controls.label: Iron content
controls.qualification: FeO estimated by the published reflectance calibration, separately from the mineral-mixture fit. Kaguya MI derived map, May 2016 release, within ±50° latitude. Colors show modeled values; gray grid marks missing data and the unmapped polar regions. The display samples native cells without filling gaps. Values outside 0–100 weight % and cells lacking a valid companion fit are masked.
controls.notes: Iron changes how lunar material reflects light. Scientists use that signal to estimate its iron content, expressed as FeO. FeO weight percent: 10% means 10 parts FeO per 100 parts of material by weight. Yellow means more; values at or above 25% share one color. A published calibration converts Kaguya’s reflected-light measurements to FeO content, separately from the mineral-mixture model. Values outside 0–100% are excluded, along with cells lacking a usable companion model fit. This is not a map of rust deposits. 50° south to 50° north. Gray grid marks the polar regions, missing measurements, or cells without a usable model fit.

controls.label: Surface weathering
controls.qualification: Optical maturity (OMAT) is a dimensionless reflectance index. Smaller values indicate more optically mature, space-weathered soil; this is not an exposure-age measurement. Kaguya MI derived map, May 2016 release, within ±50° latitude. Colors show modeled values; gray grid marks missing data and the unmapped polar regions. The display samples native cells without filling gaps. Cells lacking a valid companion fit are masked to avoid treating unqualified zeros as mature terrain.
controls.notes: Solar-wind particles and tiny impacts alter exposed soil. This measure of the change in reflected light is called optical maturity (OMAT). Lower values mean more weathered soil; higher values mean fresher material. Values at or above 0.5 share the brightest color. The published OMAT formula combines two Kaguya wavelength bands after matching them to the Clementine calibration. The index has no units and does not give an age in years. Composition also affects interpretation. 50° south to 50° north. Gray grid marks the polar regions, missing measurements, or cells without a usable model fit.
